meta.why_counts_not_names: A field added to a subset of chips slips past a names-only assertion -- page_size (2 of 746) and five sparse top-level keys (datasheet, provenance, source, verification_note, verification_status, each 2 of 746) already demonstrate this: every one of those names already exists in the frozen inventory, so a names-only check is already satisfied today, and a SIXTH chip gaining any of them would be completely invisible to it. Pinning the per-key occurrence COUNT catches that class of change; pinning only the name set cannot.
meta.why_not_diff_db: tools/diff_db.py's GATE-02 (_diff_field_paths) already unions both key sets and would see a new field, but it compares the live database against tools/baseline/chip_database.baseline.json, and regenerating that baseline silences the comparison -- anyone who lets a new field in simply re-runs the baseline generator and the diff goes quiet. This inventory is the non-silenceable half of TABLE-05's DB-side gate and is deliberately NOT derived from, or compared against, that baseline.
meta.how_to_update: Re-derive every number in this file with an independent traversal of the live chip_database.json (two levels deep: {manufacturer: [chip, ...]}) -- never hand-edit a count to make a surprise disappear. State in the commit message which key changed, on which level, and why. If tools/build_db.py's chip_entry construction or tools/extra_chips.json changed, also re-derive generator_emitted_chip_entry_keys the same way (an ast walk over chip_entry plus a key scan of extra_chips.json) rather than editing the list by hand.
meta.db_is_generated: firestarter/data/chip_database.json is produced by tools/build_db.py from the upstream tools/infoic.xml (plus the hand-curated tools/extra_chips.json supplement) and is never hand-edited, which is why this gate also reads the generator.
meta.generator_scan_scope: generator_emitted_chip_entry_keys is NOT purely an ast walk of build_db.py's `chip_entry` construction -- five of the eleven top-level keys (datasheet, provenance, source, verification_note, verification_status) are never assigned through a variable named chip_entry at all. They enter chip_database.json via the VAR-05/D-10 post-decode merge (`complete_db.setdefault(mfg, []).extend(extra_chips)`) that reads tools/extra_chips.json wholesale and appends its two hand-curated chip records verbatim. Confirmed in-session: an ast walk scoped to `chip_entry` alone finds exactly 21 names, 5 short of this file's 26 -- the missing 5 are precisely the sparse-subset keys `why_counts_not_names` warns about. The gate's live derivation is therefore the UNION of an ast walk over build_db.py's `chip_entry` construction and a key scan of tools/extra_chips.json; both paths are covered, so a new field entering through either one is caught.
